protocol.title: Independent typed response-control implementation and maintenance study
protocol.description: A preregistered 96-session comparison of four unseen authenticated, validated, conflict-aware, or creation-oriented server-plus-browser assignments in Parley, Python, TypeScript, and Rust.

validated_transport.channel: Two protected mode-0600 POSIX FIFOs carry bounded request and public-feedback messages; only the parent evaluator binds loopback.
validated_transport.threat_boundary: The transport is a measurement-integrity mechanism for command-constrained agents, not an isolation boundary against a deliberately hostile workspace process.

validated_exact_build_freeze.positive_control: Canonical manifest/lock survives native release and wasm32 release builds byte-for-byte.
validated_exact_build_freeze.negative_control: A displaced root block passes cargo metadata --locked --offline; cargo build --release returns zero and rewrites it; post-command hashes reject the build.
validated_exact_build_freeze.required_integration: Reference validation and measured evaluation must hash every protected/read-only input immediately after each exact build command for every language, in addition to final workspace integrity.

scratch_space_control.preflight_timing: Resolve disjoint work, journal, and attempt roots and require the full four-worker budget before journal initialization or any measured cell start.
scratch_space_control.evidence_boundary: The disposable work root and durable journal/attempt roots must be distinct real directories with no equal, ancestor, or descendant relationship.
scratch_space_control.cleanup_order: Persist the complete finished journal and external parent attempts before removing that journal's exact real immediate-child workspace through cleanup_finished_workspace.
scratch_space_control.resume_policy: On resume, seal every started unfinished cell as a permanent failure before reclaiming only workspaces certified by finished records; run only never-started cells.
scratch_space_control.failure_policy: Preflight, boundary, cleanup, or renewed capacity failure stops scheduling new cells, remains an execution-integrity failure after any cell starts, and never authorizes a rerun.
scratch_space_control.calibration_rule: Clean-room harness validation must measure peak per-cell scratch use. Revision 2 may increase, but never lower, the frozen reserve or per-worker budget before the first measured session.

matrix.derivation: 4 tasks x 4 languages x 2 agent configurations x 3 replicates

parley.stack: Generated native HTTP/JSON server with checked dynamic response envelopes, dependency-free strict route codecs, and generated browser WebAssembly bindings
parley.agent_context: Frozen 313-token v0.5.6 scaffolded response-web card used alone and included in measured input tokens.

python.stack: FastAPI 0.141.1, Uvicorn 0.52.1, Pydantic 2.13.4, and a counted browser JavaScript application module

rust.stack: Axum 0.8.9, Tokio 1.53.1, Tower HTTP 0.7.0, Serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151, and a scalar WebAssembly export

scaffold_protocol.purpose: Supply stable language-appropriate transport, build, and browser wiring so the measured assignment is application implementation or repair rather than framework installation.
scaffold_protocol.editable: All task-specific application logic, typed request/body/response envelope declarations, authorization/validation/conflict handlers, browser rule modules, and application manifests required by that language.
scaffold_protocol.read_only: Dependency locks, generic launch adapters, shared static shell, frozen contract, source printer, generated check client, public check wrapper, and benchmark configuration.
scaffold_protocol.source_visibility: The first shell command prints every editable and visibly read-only source/context file exactly once. Direct reconnaissance or reading protected case/configuration files is forbidden.
scaffold_protocol.dependency_setup: Pinned dependencies are installed or fetched before measured sessions. Each parent evaluation uses only the frozen local dependency store; network time is never part of a cell.
scaffold_protocol.reference_validation: Before any agent session, an isolated reference application for every task/language must run the exact measured build commands under post-command hash checks, preserve all protected/read-only inputs, and pass every public and hidden HTTP status/JSON/custom-header plus browser case. Seeded maintenance applications must build with stable hashes, fail their public response-control case, and pass after changing only the predeclared route-handler root file.
scaffold_protocol.rust_lockfile: Generate Cargo.lock canonically from the final fullstack-agent-045 manifest. Run cargo build --locked --offline --release and the exact wasm32 release build under immediate post-command hash checks before execution freeze, and preserve that reviewed hash in every measured workspace.
scaffold_protocol.symmetry: Every language receives the same English contract and semantic cases. Framework-specific source and configuration may differ, but no language receives a hidden expected value or repair.

session_protocol.runner: A new iteration-045 runner creates one isolated workspace, one external attempt directory, one immutable journal entry, and one ephemeral Codex thread per cell; it must not modify historical runners.
session_protocol.tool_policy: Disable user configuration, repository rules, plugins, apps, browser-use, computer-use, and multi-agent delegation. Use workspace-write with approval never and network disabled.
session_protocol.command_policy: The first shell command must be exactly ./sources and occur once. Every later shell command must be exactly ./check. At least one and at most twelve ./check commands are permitted.
session_protocol.public_feedback: Each ./check request is evaluated by the parent outside the sandbox. It records build output and exact public HTTP status/JSON/custom-header plus real-Chromium verdicts, then returns only bounded public feedback.
session_protocol.public_execution_requirement: Every completed public attempt must actually execute all four public cases, including the declared browser case. A build failure may short-circuit cases but remains a recorded failed attempt; zero semantic case execution cannot count as a passing check.
session_protocol.hidden_judgment: After the agent exits, the parent separately rebuilds final source and executes all withheld HTTP status/JSON/custom-header and browser cases. Hidden inputs and values never enter the workspace or public transport.
session_protocol.attempt_capture: Preserve every parent-owned public attempt, source snapshot, file hash, changed-file list, command event, agent message, diagnostic, stdout/stderr, elapsed time, thread ID, and reported token count.
session_protocol.integrity: Hash all protected/read-only files immediately after every exact build and at cell finalization; reject unexpected files and symlinks; compare FIFO device/inode/type/mode/owner; revalidate frozen repository and toolchain provenance; require one start/finish journal record per cell; preserve the initial and renewed scratch checks without binding observed free bytes into resume identity; persist evidence and measured workspace bytes before bounded per-cell cleanup.
session_protocol.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; only never-started cells may execute.
session_protocol.failure_policy: Timeouts, interruptions, agent errors, nonzero exits, build failures, case failures, protocol violations, checker/FIFO/read-only integrity failures, missing source, unexpected files, scratch-boundary violations, low-space events after start, and cleanup failures are failures and remain in the complete result.
session_protocol.domain_judgment: The parent validates JSON syntax and declared JSON types but does not pre-reject negative integers or zero-capacity combinations. Those typed values must reach every language handler and receive the frozen 422 envelope.

execution_freeze.description: Post-protocol response-control harness, transparent proxy, v0.5.6 compact-context integration, scratch lifecycle, and exact-build execution inputs frozen after clean-room validation and before the first measured cell; all task, case, expected status/JSON/header/browser, model, metric, threshold, gate, compiler, context, and stack semantics are unchanged.
execution_freeze.public_attempt_storage: Atomic JSON files outside the agent workspace, revalidated during cell finalization and result aggregation.
execution_freeze.scratch_preflight: 17,179,869,184 bytes free required before journal initialization and every scheduling refill with work/journal/attempt roots proven disjoint; observed capacity is evidence rather than resume identity.
execution_freeze.workspace_cleanup: A separate immutable cleanup record is written only after the complete finished journal; it retains pre-cleanup workspace bytes and proves removal, absence, or permanent cleanup failure.
execution_freeze.bounded_scheduler: At most four cells are active and no later cell is queued; a run-level capacity or cleanup failure stops refills and permanently journals all unstarted cells as failed without creating agent sessions.
execution_freeze.response_proxy: Identical transparent parent-owned loopback proxy for all languages; it forwards typed negative/zero domain inputs and preserves application headers while normalizing framing.
execution_freeze.application_header_judgment: Compare the complete normalized multiset of non-server, non-hop-by-hop response header pairs; missing, extra, wrong, or duplicate application headers fail.
execution_freeze.exact_build_integrity: Every protected/read-only file is checked before and immediately after each exact build command; any mutation fails the build and cell.
execution_freeze.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; finished evidence is reconciled with cleanup evidence; only never-started cells may execute.

metrics.correctness: Exact hidden HTTP status/JSON/error/custom application headers and real-browser scalar results, overall and by task, kind, language, model, and replicate.
metrics.first_check: Whether the first parent-owned public build and all four public cases pass, with HTTP and browser execution counts retained.
metrics.repairs: Number of later ./check attempts after the first, with every parent attempt retained outside the workspace.
metrics.tokens: Complete reported Codex input, cached input, uncached input, output, reasoning output, and input-plus-output totals. Primary efficiency uses complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment.
metrics.elapsed: Monotonic wall time for the whole fresh session, including parent-owned public builds and repairs but excluding dependency installation.
metrics.maintainability: Changed editable files, rough token edit size, and whether maintenance patches touch exactly the predeclared defect-root file set.
metrics.source: Final and seed UTF-8 bytes, physical lines, rough tokens, o200k_base tokens, and per-file SHA-256, reported descriptively rather than substituted for session tokens.
metrics.cross_target: Authorized/domain-valid HTTP/browser equality for the shared scalar plus successful Chromium execution; status/header branches remain separately exact.

primary_gate.execution_integrity: A preregistered scratch preflight must pass before journaling; all 96 cells must finish exactly once with unique thread IDs, exactly one journal start/finish, durable evidence before bounded workspace cleanup, intact repository/toolchain/checker/read-only/FIFO state including post-build hashes, compliant commands, required public HTTP/browser execution, no runner or cleanup error, and no selective rerun or exclusion.
primary_gate.correctness: Parley must pass 100% of hidden HTTP status/JSON/custom-header and browser cases, and its assignment success rate must be no lower than every baseline overall, within each agent configuration, and within implementation and maintenance tasks.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley's first-public-check assignment success rate must be no lower than the highest baseline rate overall and within each task kind.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley's median complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley's median elapsed seconds per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.maintainability: Every hidden-correct Parley maintenance assignment must change exactly its predeclared root file set, and its exact-root rate must be no lower than every baseline.
primary_gate.verdict: All six conditions must hold for strict unseen full-stack agent parity/efficiency. Report every condition independently even when the overall gate fails.

secondary_analysis: Report full distributions, paired task/configuration/replicate cells, and per-task outcomes; do not replace the primary result with successful, repair-free, or model-selected subsets.
Report implementation and maintenance separately, including root-file quality, public/hidden HTTP-browser execution, and disagreement classes.
Report both model configurations separately before any pooled interpretation.
Report public-attempt counts and public case executions so a build-only or browser-skipped check cannot be mistaken for semantic feedback.
Report post-build protected/read-only hash checks by language and build phase; do not collapse them into only the final workspace flag.
Report scratch preflight, peak per-cell/worker usage, each evidence-gated cleanup, and final free space; never delete durable evidence to improve a result.
Compare studies 036–044 only as motivation and mechanism history. Do not combine their task results, tokens, or timing with 045.
Classify failures after preserving the frozen outcome; classification cannot change a verdict.
interpretation_boundary: The study covers four small synthetic response-control plus browser contracts, two model IDs, one reasoning setting, and one frozen toolchain environment.
Stack scaffolds test application work, not framework discovery, dependency selection, deployment, sustained load, databases, accessibility, or production operations.
Bearer/API-key comparisons test typed authorization decisions and headers, not identity-provider, credential-storage, cryptographic, session, or policy-system security.
Framework source and compiler implementations are infrastructure. Application-facing context is preserved, while complete session tokens remain primary cost.
A deterministic scalar ES-module export in real Chromium is a cross-target check, not a general user-interface evaluation.
Synthetic route-handler defects measure only the declared boundary behaviors and do not estimate production-defect distributions.
Even a fully passing gate cannot prove universal language superiority; it supports only the frozen comparative claim.
A failed strict gate remains useful evidence and cannot be repaired by same-corpus language, context, prompt, task, runner, threshold, or metric tuning.
protocol.implementation_rule: Scaffolds, reference applications, dependency preparation, and the runner are implemented only after this protocol commit. Their exact hashes and clean-room evidence must be committed in revision 2 before measurement.
protocol.change_rule: From corpus commit 3f3a5943532cd63a151ec8221715f75ab352a931 onward, no task, case, expected value/status/header, language semantics, compiler, context, metric, threshold, model, reasoning setting, replicate count, or primary gate may change based on scaffolds, reference validation, smoke checks, or measured output. An objective harness defect may be corrected only before measurement in a documented zero-session amendment preserving old commits and semantic hashes. Scratch budgets may increase but not decrease.
protocol.stop_rule: Run every frozen cell once, preserve and publish the complete result whether positive, mixed, negative, or invalid, and make no same-corpus optimization or rerun. Any later product change requires a corpus outside iteration 045.

from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid',strict=True); bid_key:str; solar_arrays:int; wind_turbines:int; storage_banks:int; interconnects:int; emergency_mode:bool; duplicate_bid:bool
def score(solar_arrays:int,wind_turbines:int,storage_banks:int,interconnects:int,emergency_mode:bool)->int:
    generation=solar_arrays*9+wind_turbines*13
    buffer=storage_banks*(7 if emergency_mode else 3)
    required=generation+buffer
    capacity=interconnects*55
    delivered=min(required,capacity)
    shortfall=max(required-capacity,0)
    return delivered+shortfall*4+(required//31)*9
def calculate(v:RequestInput)->dict[str,object]:
    generation=v.solar_arrays*9+v.wind_turbines*13; buffer=v.storage_banks*(7 if v.emergency_mode else 3); required=generation+buffer; capacity=v.interconnects*55; shortfall=max(required-capacity,0)
    return {'bid_key':v.bid_key,'generation_units':generation,'battery_buffer_units':buffer,'grid_required_units':required,'grid_capacity_units':capacity,'delivered_units':min(required,capacity),'shortfall_units':shortfall,'dispatch_windows':required//31,'bid_score':score(v.solar_arrays,v.wind_turbines,v.storage_banks,v.interconnects,v.emergency_mode),'bid_state':'accepted' if shortfall==0 else 'emergency_shortfall' if v.emergency_mode else 'routine_shortfall'}

logic.par.text:
to trail_permit_score with day_hikers as number, overnight_hikers as number, trail_guides as number, storm_alert as yesno giving number:
    let required be day_hikers times 5 plus overnight_hikers times 12
    if storm_alert:
        set required to required plus trail_guides times 6
    let capacity be trail_guides times 38
    let admitted be required
    if admitted is more than capacity:
        set admitted to capacity
    let waiting be required minus capacity
    if waiting is less than 0:
        set waiting to 0
    give back admitted plus waiting times 6

main.par.text:
include "logic.par"
a web_request has method as text, path as text, query as text, headers as map from text to text, body as text
a request_input has permit_code as text, day_hikers as number, overnight_hikers as number, trail_guides as number, storm_alert as yesno
a response_body has permit_code as text, visitor_total as number, trail_units as number, guide_capacity_units as number, admitted_units as number, waiting_units as number, permit_score as number, permit_state as text
a controlled_response has status as number, headers as map from text to text, body as response_body
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Trail Permit", ready yes
to empty_body with key as text, state as text giving response_body:
    give back a response_body with permit_code key, visitor_total 0, trail_units 0, guide_capacity_units 0, admitted_units 0, waiting_units 0, permit_score 0, permit_state state
to handle_request with request as web_request, body as request_input giving controlled_response:
    let headers be a map from text to text
    let credential be (maybe item "authorization" of request's headers) otherwise ""
    if credential is not "Bearer trail-045":
        set item "www-authenticate" of headers to "Bearer realm=trail-permit"
        give back a controlled_response with status 401, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's permit_code, "authorization_required")
    if body's day_hikers is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's permit_code, "invalid")
    if body's overnight_hikers is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's permit_code, "invalid")
    if body's trail_guides is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's permit_code, "invalid")
    if body's trail_guides is 0:
        if body's day_hikers plus body's overnight_hikers is more than 0:
            set item "x-validation" of headers to "trail_guides"
            give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's permit_code, "invalid")
    let total be body's day_hikers plus body's overnight_hikers
    let required be body's day_hikers times 5 plus body's overnight_hikers times 12
    if body's storm_alert:
        set required to required plus body's trail_guides times 6
    let capacity be body's trail_guides times 38
    let admitted be required
    if admitted is more than capacity:
        set admitted to capacity
    let waiting be required minus capacity
    if waiting is less than 0:
        set waiting to 0
    let state be "issued"
    if waiting is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_queue"
        if body's storm_alert:
            set state to "storm_queue"
    let result be a response_body with permit_code body's permit_code, visitor_total total, trail_units required, guide_capacity_units capacity, admitted_units admitted, waiting_units waiting, permit_score (trail_permit_score with body's day_hikers, body's overnight_hikers, body's trail_guides, body's storm_alert), permit_state state
    set item "x-permit-state" of headers to state
    give back a controlled_response with status 200, headers headers, body result

# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid',strict=True); booking_code:str; chilled_crates:int; frozen_crates:int; loading_docks:int; rush_load:bool
def score(chilled_crates:int,frozen_crates:int,loading_docks:int,rush_load:bool)->int:
    total=chilled_crates+frozen_crates; required=chilled_crates*7+frozen_crates*15+(loading_docks*5 if rush_load else 0); capacity=loading_docks*44
    return min(required,capacity)+max(required-capacity,0)*5+(total//6)*8
def calculate(v:RequestInput)->dict[str,object]:
    total=v.chilled_crates+v.frozen_crates; required=v.chilled_crates*7+v.frozen_crates*15+(v.loading_docks*5 if v.rush_load else 0); capacity=v.loading_docks*44; deferred=max(required-capacity,0)
    return {'booking_code':v.booking_code,'shipment_total':total,'cooling_units':required,'dock_capacity_units':capacity,'loaded_units':min(required,capacity),'deferred_units':deferred,'loading_rounds':total//6,'booking_score':score(v.chilled_crates,v.frozen_crates,v.loading_docks,v.rush_load),'booking_state':'booked' if deferred==0 else 'rush_queue' if v.rush_load else 'routine_queue'}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair authorization polarity in a trail permit workflow

    Repair the supplied Trail Permit application. The POST route requires Authorization: Bearer trail-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate Bearer realm=trail-permit and permit_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive visitor_total with zero trail_guides returns 422 with x-validation trail_guides. Otherwise visitor_total is day_hikers + overnight_hikers. trail_units is day_hikers * 5 + overnight_hikers * 12 plus trail_guides * 6 during storm_alert. guide_capacity_units is trail_guides * 38. admitted_units is min(trail_units, capacity). waiting_units is max(trail_units - capacity, 0). permit_score is admitted_units + waiting_units * 6. permit_state is issued when waiting is zero, storm_queue during a storm, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 200 with x-permit-state. The browser export returns permit_score. Failure bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/trail-permit-ready` returns `{"service":"Trail Permit","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/trail-permits` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `day_hikers`: number
- `overnight_hikers`: number
- `trail_guides`: number
- `storm_alert`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `visitor_total`: number
- `trail_units`: number
- `guide_capacity_units`: number
- `admitted_units`: number
- `waiting_units`: number
- `permit_score`: number
- `permit_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `trail_permit_score` with arguments in this order:
    `day_hikers, overnight_hikers, trail_guides, storm_alert`. It returns `permit_score`.

# Repair authorization polarity in a trail permit workflow

    Repair the supplied Trail Permit application. The POST route requires Authorization: Bearer trail-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate Bearer realm=trail-permit and permit_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive visitor_total with zero trail_guides returns 422 with x-validation trail_guides. Otherwise visitor_total is day_hikers + overnight_hikers. trail_units is day_hikers * 5 + overnight_hikers * 12 plus trail_guides * 6 during storm_alert. guide_capacity_units is trail_guides * 38. admitted_units is min(trail_units, capacity). waiting_units is max(trail_units - capacity, 0). permit_score is admitted_units + waiting_units * 6. permit_state is issued when waiting is zero, storm_queue during a storm, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 200 with x-permit-state. The browser export returns permit_score. Failure bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/trail-permit-ready` returns `{"service":"Trail Permit","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/trail-permits` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `day_hikers`: number
- `overnight_hikers`: number
- `trail_guides`: number
- `storm_alert`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `visitor_total`: number
- `trail_units`: number
- `guide_capacity_units`: number
- `admitted_units`: number
- `waiting_units`: number
- `permit_score`: number
- `permit_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `trail_permit_score` with arguments in this order:
    `day_hikers, overnight_hikers, trail_guides, storm_alert`. It returns `permit_score`.

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build an authenticated asynchronous microgrid bid workflow

    Implement the frozen Microgrid Bid contract. The POST route requires x-grid-key: grid-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate GridKey and bid_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive generation with zero interconnects returns 422 with x-validation interconnects. A duplicate_bid returns 409 with x-conflict duplicate_bid. Otherwise generation_units is solar_arrays * 9 + wind_turbines * 13. battery_buffer_units is storage_banks * 7 during emergency_mode and storage_banks * 3 otherwise. grid_required_units is generation + buffer. grid_capacity_units is interconnects * 55. delivered_units is the minimum of required and capacity. shortfall_units is max(required - capacity, 0). dispatch_windows is grid_required_units divided by 31 using floor division. bid_score is delivered_units + shortfall_units * 4 + dispatch_windows * 9. bid_state is accepted when shortfall is zero, emergency_shortfall during emergency mode, and routine_shortfall otherwise. Success returns 202 with location /api/v9/microgrid-bids/{bid_key}, retry-after 3, and x-bid-state. The browser export returns bid_score. Failure bodies use the request key and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/microgrid-bid-ready` returns `{"service":"Microgrid Bid","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/microgrid-bids` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `bid_key`: text
- `solar_arrays`: number
- `wind_turbines`: number
- `storage_banks`: number
- `interconnects`: number
- `emergency_mode`: yesno
- `duplicate_bid`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `bid_key`: text
- `generation_units`: number
- `battery_buffer_units`: number
- `grid_required_units`: number
- `grid_capacity_units`: number
- `delivered_units`: number
- `shortfall_units`: number
- `dispatch_windows`: number
- `bid_score`: number
- `bid_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `microgrid_bid_score` with arguments in this order:
    `solar_arrays, wind_turbines, storage_banks, interconnects, emergency_mode`. It returns `bid_score`.

# Build an authenticated asynchronous microgrid bid workflow

    Implement the frozen Microgrid Bid contract. The POST route requires x-grid-key: grid-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate GridKey and bid_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive generation with zero interconnects returns 422 with x-validation interconnects. A duplicate_bid returns 409 with x-conflict duplicate_bid. Otherwise generation_units is solar_arrays * 9 + wind_turbines * 13. battery_buffer_units is storage_banks * 7 during emergency_mode and storage_banks * 3 otherwise. grid_required_units is generation + buffer. grid_capacity_units is interconnects * 55. delivered_units is the minimum of required and capacity. shortfall_units is max(required - capacity, 0). dispatch_windows is grid_required_units divided by 31 using floor division. bid_score is delivered_units + shortfall_units * 4 + dispatch_windows * 9. bid_state is accepted when shortfall is zero, emergency_shortfall during emergency mode, and routine_shortfall otherwise. Success returns 202 with location /api/v9/microgrid-bids/{bid_key}, retry-after 3, and x-bid-state. The browser export returns bid_score. Failure bodies use the request key and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/microgrid-bid-ready` returns `{"service":"Microgrid Bid","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/microgrid-bids` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `bid_key`: text
- `solar_arrays`: number
- `wind_turbines`: number
- `storage_banks`: number
- `interconnects`: number
- `emergency_mode`: yesno
- `duplicate_bid`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `bid_key`: text
- `generation_units`: number
- `battery_buffer_units`: number
- `grid_required_units`: number
- `grid_capacity_units`: number
- `delivered_units`: number
- `shortfall_units`: number
- `dispatch_windows`: number
- `bid_score`: number
- `bid_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `microgrid_bid_score` with arguments in this order:
    `solar_arrays, wind_turbines, storage_banks, interconnects, emergency_mode`. It returns `bid_score`.

from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid',strict=True); bid_key:str; solar_arrays:int; wind_turbines:int; storage_banks:int; interconnects:int; emergency_mode:bool; duplicate_bid:bool
def score(solar_arrays:int,wind_turbines:int,storage_banks:int,interconnects:int,emergency_mode:bool)->int:
    generation=solar_arrays*9+wind_turbines*13
    buffer=storage_banks*(7 if emergency_mode else 3)
    required=generation+buffer
    capacity=interconnects*55
    delivered=min(required,capacity)
    shortfall=max(required-capacity,0)
    dispatch_windows=required//31
    return delivered+shortfall*4+dispatch_windows*9
def calculate(v:RequestInput)->dict[str,object]:
    generation=v.solar_arrays*9+v.wind_turbines*13; buffer=v.storage_banks*(7 if v.emergency_mode else 3); required=generation+buffer; capacity=v.interconnects*55; shortfall=max(required-capacity,0)
    return {'bid_key':v.bid_key,'generation_units':generation,'battery_buffer_units':buffer,'grid_required_units':required,'grid_capacity_units':capacity,'delivered_units':min(required,capacity),'shortfall_units':shortfall,'dispatch_windows':required//31,'bid_score':score(v.solar_arrays,v.wind_turbines,v.storage_banks,v.interconnects,v.emergency_mode),'bid_state':'accepted' if shortfall==0 else 'emergency_shortfall' if v.emergency_mode else 'routine_shortfall'}

Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};#[derive(Deserialize)]#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]pub struct RequestInput{pub booking_code:String,pub chilled_crates:i64,pub frozen_crates:i64,pub loading_docks:i64,pub rush_load:bool}#[derive(Serialize)]pub struct ResponseOutput{pub booking_code:String,pub shipment_total:i64,pub cooling_units:i64,pub dock_capacity_units:i64,pub loaded_units:i64,pub deferred_units:i64,pub loading_rounds:i64,pub booking_score:i64,pub booking_state:String}pub fn score(a:i64,b:i64,d:i64,r:bool)->i64{let t=a+b;let x=a*7+b*15+if r{d*5}else{0};let c=d*44;x.min(c)+(x-c).max(0)*5+(t/6)*8}pub fn calculate(v:&RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let t=v.chilled_crates+v.frozen_crates;let x=v.chilled_crates*7+v.frozen_crates*15+if v.rush_load{v.loading_docks*5}else{0};let c=v.loading_docks*44;let d=(x-c).max(0);ResponseOutput{booking_code:v.booking_code.clone(),shipment_total:t,cooling_units:x,dock_capacity_units:c,loaded_units:x.min(c),deferred_units:d,loading_rounds:t/6,booking_score:score(v.chilled_crates,v.frozen_crates,v.loading_docks,v.rush_load),booking_state:if d==0{"booked"}else if v.rush_load{"rush_queue"}else{"routine_queue"}.into()}}#[unsafe(no_mangle)]pub extern "C" fn parley_browser_score(a0:i64,a1:i64,a2:i64,a3:i32)->i64{score(a0,a1,a2,a3!=0)}

# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid',strict=True); booking_code:str; chilled_crates:int; frozen_crates:int; loading_docks:int; rush_load:bool
def score(chilled_crates:int,frozen_crates:int,loading_docks:int,rush_load:bool)->int:
    total=chilled_crates+frozen_crates; required=chilled_crates*7+frozen_crates*15+(loading_docks*5 if rush_load else 0); capacity=loading_docks*44
    return min(required,capacity)+max(required-capacity,0)*5+(total//6)*8
def calculate(v:RequestInput)->dict[str,object]:
    total=v.chilled_crates+v.frozen_crates; required=v.chilled_crates*7+v.frozen_crates*15+(v.loading_docks*5 if v.rush_load else 0); capacity=v.loading_docks*44; deferred=max(required-capacity,0)
    return {'booking_code':v.booking_code,'shipment_total':total,'cooling_units':required,'dock_capacity_units':capacity,'loaded_units':min(required,capacity),'deferred_units':deferred,'loading_rounds':total//6,'booking_score':score(v.chilled_crates,v.frozen_crates,v.loading_docks,v.rush_load),'booking_state':'booked' if deferred==0 else 'rush_queue' if v.rush_load else 'routine_queue'}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build an authenticated asynchronous microgrid bid workflow

    Implement the frozen Microgrid Bid contract. The POST route requires x-grid-key: grid-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate GridKey and bid_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive generation with zero interconnects returns 422 with x-validation interconnects. A duplicate_bid returns 409 with x-conflict duplicate_bid. Otherwise generation_units is solar_arrays * 9 + wind_turbines * 13. battery_buffer_units is storage_banks * 7 during emergency_mode and storage_banks * 3 otherwise. grid_required_units is generation + buffer. grid_capacity_units is interconnects * 55. delivered_units is the minimum of required and capacity. shortfall_units is max(required - capacity, 0). dispatch_windows is grid_required_units divided by 31 using floor division. bid_score is delivered_units + shortfall_units * 4 + dispatch_windows * 9. bid_state is accepted when shortfall is zero, emergency_shortfall during emergency mode, and routine_shortfall otherwise. Success returns 202 with location /api/v9/microgrid-bids/{bid_key}, retry-after 3, and x-bid-state. The browser export returns bid_score. Failure bodies use the request key and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/microgrid-bid-ready` returns `{"service":"Microgrid Bid","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/microgrid-bids` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `bid_key`: text
- `solar_arrays`: number
- `wind_turbines`: number
- `storage_banks`: number
- `interconnects`: number
- `emergency_mode`: yesno
- `duplicate_bid`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `bid_key`: text
- `generation_units`: number
- `battery_buffer_units`: number
- `grid_required_units`: number
- `grid_capacity_units`: number
- `delivered_units`: number
- `shortfall_units`: number
- `dispatch_windows`: number
- `bid_score`: number
- `bid_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `microgrid_bid_score` with arguments in this order:
    `solar_arrays, wind_turbines, storage_banks, interconnects, emergency_mode`. It returns `bid_score`.

a response_body has bid_key as text, generation_units as number, battery_buffer_units as number, grid_required_units as number, grid_capacity_units as number, delivered_units as number, shortfall_units as number, dispatch_windows as number, bid_score as number, bid_state as text
a controlled_response has status as number, headers as map from text to text, body as response_body
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Microgrid Bid", ready yes
to empty_body with key as text, state as text giving response_body:
    give back a response_body with bid_key key, generation_units 0, battery_buffer_units 0, grid_required_units 0, grid_capacity_units 0, delivered_units 0, shortfall_units 0, dispatch_windows 0, bid_score 0, bid_state state
to handle_request with request as web_request, body as request_input giving controlled_response:
    let headers be a map from text to text
    let credential be (maybe item "x-grid-key" of request's headers) otherwise ""
    if credential is not "grid-045":
        set item "www-authenticate" of headers to "GridKey"
        give back a controlled_response with status 401, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "authorization_required")
    if body's solar_arrays is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's wind_turbines is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's storage_banks is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's interconnects is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's interconnects is 0:
        if body's solar_arrays times 9 plus body's wind_turbines times 13 is more than 0:
            set item "x-validation" of headers to "interconnects"
            give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's duplicate_bid:
        set item "x-conflict" of headers to "duplicate_bid"
        give back a controlled_response with status 409, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "duplicate")
    let generation be body's solar_arrays times 9 plus body's wind_turbines times 13
    let buffer be body's storage_banks times 3
    if body's emergency_mode:
        set buffer to body's storage_banks times 7
    let required be generation plus buffer
    let capacity be body's interconnects times 55
    let delivered be required
    if delivered is more than capacity:
        set delivered to capacity
    let shortfall be required minus capacity
    if shortfall is less than 0:
        set shortfall to 0
    let windows be number from (required divided by 31)
    let state be "accepted"
    if shortfall is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_shortfall"
        if body's emergency_mode:
            set state to "emergency_shortfall"
    let result be a response_body with bid_key body's bid_key, generation_units generation, battery_buffer_units buffer, grid_required_units required, grid_capacity_units capacity, delivered_units delivered, shortfall_units shortfall, dispatch_windows windows, bid_score (microgrid_bid_score with body's solar_arrays, body's wind_turbines, body's storage_banks, body's interconnects, body's emergency_mode), bid_state state
    give back a controlled_response with status 200, headers headers, body result

    let deferred be cooling minus capacity
    if deferred is less than 0:

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

# Repair a server-owned header in a cold-chain booking workflow

    Repair the supplied Cold-Chain Booking application. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive shipment_total with zero loading_docks returns 422 with x-validation loading_docks. Otherwise shipment_total is chilled_crates + frozen_crates. cooling_units is chilled_crates * 7 + frozen_crates * 15 plus loading_docks * 5 during rush_load. dock_capacity_units is loading_docks * 44. loaded_units is min(cooling_units, capacity). deferred_units is max(cooling_units - capacity, 0). loading_rounds is shipment_total divided by 6 using floor division. booking_score is loaded_units + deferred_units * 5 + loading_rounds * 8. booking_state is booked when deferred is zero, rush_queue during rush load, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{booking_code} and x-booking-state. The browser export returns booking_score. Validation bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/cold-chain-booking-ready` returns `{"service":"Cold-Chain Booking","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/cold-chain-bookings` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `chilled_crates`: number
- `frozen_crates`: number
- `loading_docks`: number
- `rush_load`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `booking_code`: text
- `shipment_total`: number
- `cooling_units`: number
- `dock_capacity_units`: number
- `loaded_units`: number
- `deferred_units`: number
- `loading_rounds`: number
- `booking_score`: number
- `booking_state`: text

    Export `cold_chain_booking_score` with arguments in this order:
    `chilled_crates, frozen_crates, loading_docks, rush_load`. It returns `booking_score`.

to cold_chain_booking_score with chilled_crates as number, frozen_crates as number, loading_docks as number, rush_load as yesno giving number:
    let cooling be chilled_crates times 7 plus frozen_crates times 15
    if rush_load:
        set cooling to cooling plus loading_docks times 5
    let capacity be loading_docks times 44
    let loaded be cooling
    if loaded is more than capacity:
        set loaded to capacity
    let deferred be cooling minus capacity
    if deferred is less than 0:
        set deferred to 0
    give back loaded plus deferred times 5 plus number from ((chilled_crates plus frozen_crates) divided by 6) times 8

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair authorization polarity in a trail permit workflow

    Repair the supplied Trail Permit application. The POST route requires Authorization: Bearer trail-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate Bearer realm=trail-permit and permit_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive visitor_total with zero trail_guides returns 422 with x-validation trail_guides. Otherwise visitor_total is day_hikers + overnight_hikers. trail_units is day_hikers * 5 + overnight_hikers * 12 plus trail_guides * 6 during storm_alert. guide_capacity_units is trail_guides * 38. admitted_units is min(trail_units, capacity). waiting_units is max(trail_units - capacity, 0). permit_score is admitted_units + waiting_units * 6. permit_state is issued when waiting is zero, storm_queue during a storm, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 200 with x-permit-state. The browser export returns permit_score. Failure bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/trail-permit-ready` returns `{"service":"Trail Permit","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/trail-permits` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `day_hikers`: number
- `overnight_hikers`: number
- `trail_guides`: number
- `storm_alert`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `visitor_total`: number
- `trail_units`: number
- `guide_capacity_units`: number
- `admitted_units`: number
- `waiting_units`: number
- `permit_score`: number
- `permit_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `trail_permit_score` with arguments in this order:
    `day_hikers, overnight_hikers, trail_guides, storm_alert`. It returns `permit_score`.

# Repair authorization polarity in a trail permit workflow

    Repair the supplied Trail Permit application. The POST route requires Authorization: Bearer trail-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate Bearer realm=trail-permit and permit_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive visitor_total with zero trail_guides returns 422 with x-validation trail_guides. Otherwise visitor_total is day_hikers + overnight_hikers. trail_units is day_hikers * 5 + overnight_hikers * 12 plus trail_guides * 6 during storm_alert. guide_capacity_units is trail_guides * 38. admitted_units is min(trail_units, capacity). waiting_units is max(trail_units - capacity, 0). permit_score is admitted_units + waiting_units * 6. permit_state is issued when waiting is zero, storm_queue during a storm, and routine_queue otherwise. Success returns 200 with x-permit-state. The browser export returns permit_score. Failure bodies use the request code and zero numeric fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/trail-permit-ready` returns `{"service":"Trail Permit","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/trail-permits` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `day_hikers`: number
- `overnight_hikers`: number
- `trail_guides`: number
- `storm_alert`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `permit_code`: text
- `visitor_total`: number
- `trail_units`: number
- `guide_capacity_units`: number
- `admitted_units`: number
- `waiting_units`: number
- `permit_score`: number
- `permit_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `trail_permit_score` with arguments in this order:
    `day_hikers, overnight_hikers, trail_guides, storm_alert`. It returns `permit_score`.

logic.par.text:
to microgrid_bid_score with solar_arrays as number, wind_turbines as number, storage_banks as number, interconnects as number, emergency_mode as yesno giving number:
    let generation be solar_arrays times 9 plus wind_turbines times 13
    let buffer be storage_banks times 3
    if emergency_mode:
        set buffer to storage_banks times 7
    let required be generation plus buffer
    let capacity be interconnects times 55
    let delivered be required
    if delivered is more than capacity:
        set delivered to capacity
    let shortfall be required minus capacity
    if shortfall is less than 0:
        set shortfall to 0
    let windows be number from (required divided by 31)
    give back delivered plus shortfall times 4 plus windows times 9

main.par.text:
include "logic.par"
a web_request has method as text, path as text, query as text, headers as map from text to text, body as text
a request_input has bid_key as text, solar_arrays as number, wind_turbines as number, storage_banks as number, interconnects as number, emergency_mode as yesno, duplicate_bid as yesno
a response_body has bid_key as text, generation_units as number, battery_buffer_units as number, grid_required_units as number, grid_capacity_units as number, delivered_units as number, shortfall_units as number, dispatch_windows as number, bid_score as number, bid_state as text
a controlled_response has status as number, headers as map from text to text, body as response_body
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Microgrid Bid", ready yes
to empty_body with key as text, state as text giving response_body:
    give back a response_body with bid_key key, generation_units 0, battery_buffer_units 0, grid_required_units 0, grid_capacity_units 0, delivered_units 0, shortfall_units 0, dispatch_windows 0, bid_score 0, bid_state state
to handle_request with request as web_request, body as request_input giving controlled_response:
    let headers be a map from text to text
    let credential be (maybe item "x-grid-key" of request's headers) otherwise ""
    if credential is not "grid-045":
        set item "www-authenticate" of headers to "GridKey"
        give back a controlled_response with status 401, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "authorization_required")
    if body's solar_arrays is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's wind_turbines is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's storage_banks is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's interconnects is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's interconnects is 0:
        if body's solar_arrays times 9 plus body's wind_turbines times 13 is more than 0:
            set item "x-validation" of headers to "interconnects"
            give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "invalid")
    if body's duplicate_bid:
        set item "x-conflict" of headers to "duplicate_bid"
        give back a controlled_response with status 409, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's bid_key, "duplicate")
    let generation be body's solar_arrays times 9 plus body's wind_turbines times 13
    let buffer be body's storage_banks times 3
    if body's emergency_mode:
        set buffer to body's storage_banks times 7
    let required be generation plus buffer
    let capacity be body's interconnects times 55
    let delivered be required
    if delivered is more than capacity:
        set delivered to capacity
    let shortfall be required minus capacity
    if shortfall is less than 0:
        set shortfall to 0
    let windows be number from (required divided by 31)
    let state be "accepted"
    if shortfall is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_shortfall"
        if body's emergency_mode:
            set state to "emergency_shortfall"
    let result be a response_body with bid_key body's bid_key, generation_units generation, battery_buffer_units buffer, grid_required_units required, grid_capacity_units capacity, delivered_units delivered, shortfall_units shortfall, dispatch_windows windows, bid_score (microgrid_bid_score with body's solar_arrays, body's wind_turbines, body's storage_banks, body's interconnects, body's emergency_mode), bid_state state
    set item "location" of headers to "/api/v9/microgrid-bids/" plus body's bid_key
    set item "retry-after" of headers to "3"
    set item "x-bid-state" of headers to state
    give back a controlled_response with status 202, headers headers, body result

# Build an authenticated asynchronous microgrid bid workflow

    Implement the frozen Microgrid Bid contract. The POST route requires x-grid-key: grid-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate GridKey and bid_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. Positive generation with zero interconnects returns 422 with x-validation interconnects. A duplicate_bid returns 409 with x-conflict duplicate_bid. Otherwise generation_units is solar_arrays * 9 + wind_turbines * 13. battery_buffer_units is storage_banks * 7 during emergency_mode and storage_banks * 3 otherwise. grid_required_units is generation + buffer. grid_capacity_units is interconnects * 55. delivered_units is the minimum of required and capacity. shortfall_units is max(required - capacity, 0). dispatch_windows is grid_required_units divided by 31 using floor division. bid_score is delivered_units + shortfall_units * 4 + dispatch_windows * 9. bid_state is accepted when shortfall is zero, emergency_shortfall during emergency mode, and routine_shortfall otherwise. Success returns 202 with location /api/v9/microgrid-bids/{bid_key}, retry-after 3, and x-bid-state. The browser export returns bid_score. Failure bodies use the request key and zero numeric fields.

logic.par.text:
to artifact_priority_score with stable_units as number, fragile_units as number, packing_stations as number, expedited as yesno giving number:
    let total be stable_units plus fragile_units
    let packing be stable_units times 6 plus fragile_units times 11
    if expedited:
        set packing to packing plus packing_stations times 4
    let capacity be packing_stations times 40
    let overflow be packing minus capacity
    if overflow is less than 0:
        set overflow to 0
    let rounds be number from (total divided by 5)
    give back packing plus overflow times 5 plus rounds times 7

a web_request has method as text, path as text, query as text, headers as map from text to text, body as text

    let headers be a map from text to text
    let credential be (maybe item "authorization" of request's headers) otherwise ""
    if credential is not "Bearer accession-045":

    if body's stable_units is less than 0:

    if body's packing_stations is less than 0:
        set item "x-validation" of headers to "nonnegative"
        give back a controlled_response with status 422, headers headers, body (empty_body with body's accession_key, "invalid")

    if body's expedited:

    let capacity be body's packing_stations times 40
    let overflow be packing minus capacity
    if overflow is less than 0:
        set overflow to 0
    let rounds be number from (total divided by 5)
    let state be "accepted"
    if overflow is more than 0:
        set state to "queued"
    let result be a response_body with accession_key body's accession_key, artifact_total total, packing_units packing, capacity_units capacity, overflow_units overflow, inspection_rounds rounds, priority_score (artifact_priority_score with body's stable_units, body's fragile_units, body's packing_stations, body's expedited), accession_state state
    set item "location" of headers to "/api/v9/artifact-accessions/" plus body's accession_key

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build an authenticated artifact accession workflow

    Implement the frozen Artifact Accession contract. The POST route requires Authorization: Bearer accession-045; otherwise return 401 with www-authenticate Bearer realm=artifact-accession and accession_state authorization_required. Negative numeric inputs return 422 with x-validation nonnegative. A positive artifact_total with zero packing_stations returns 422 with x-validation packing_stations. Otherwise artifact_total is stable_units + fragile_units. packing_units is stable_units * 6 + fragile_units * 11 plus packing_stations * 4 when expedited. capacity_units is packing_stations * 40. overflow_units is max(packing_units - capacity_units, 0). inspection_rounds is artifact_total divided by 5 using floor division. priority_score is packing_units + overflow_units * 5 + inspection_rounds * 7. accession_state is accepted when overflow is zero and queued otherwise. Success returns 201 with location /api/v9/artifact-accessions/{accession_key} and x-accession-state. The browser export returns priority_score. Failure bodies use the request key and zero for all numeric result fields.

    ## HTTP

    - `GET /status/artifact-accession-ready` returns `{"service":"Artifact Accession","ready":true}`.
    - `POST /api/v9/artifact-accessions` uses strict JSON, then the application decides authorization,
      domain validation, status, response headers, and body.
    - Missing, unknown, or wrongly typed JSON fields return 400 `invalid_json` before the handler.
    - Negative integers are well-typed and must reach the handler's 422 decision.
    - Non-JSON POSTs return 415; bodies above 16384 bytes return 413.

    Request fields:

    - `accession_key`: text
- `stable_units`: number
- `fragile_units`: number
- `packing_stations`: number
- `expedited`: yesno

    Response fields:

    - `accession_key`: text
- `artifact_total`: number
- `packing_units`: number
- `capacity_units`: number
- `overflow_units`: number
- `inspection_rounds`: number
- `priority_score`: number
- `accession_state`: text

    ## Browser

    Export `artifact_priority_score` with arguments in this order:
    `stable_units, fragile_units, packing_stations, expedited`. It returns `priority_score`.

from __future__ import annotations
import json,os
from pathlib import Path
from fastapi import FastAPI,Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse,JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError
from logic import RequestInput,calculate
def zero(v:RequestInput,state:str)->dict[str,object]: return {'booking_code':v.booking_code,'shipment_total':0,'cooling_units':0,'dock_capacity_units':0,'loaded_units':0,'deferred_units':0,'loading_rounds':0,'booking_score':0,'booking_state':state}
def decide(v:RequestInput,request:Request)->JSONResponse:
    if any(item < 0 for item in (v.chilled_crates,v.frozen_crates,v.loading_docks,)): return outcome(zero(v,'invalid'),422,{'x-validation':'nonnegative'})
    if v.loading_docks==0 and v.chilled_crates+v.frozen_crates>0: return outcome(zero(v,'invalid'),422,{'x-validation':'loading_docks'})
    body=calculate(v); return outcome(body,201,{'content-length':f'/api/v9/cold-chain-bookings/{v.booking_code}','x-booking-state':str(body['booking_state'])})

MAX_BODY_BYTES=16_384
PUBLIC=Path(__file__).with_name('public')
def error(code:str,status:int,detail:str)->JSONResponse: return JSONResponse({'error':code,'detail':detail},status_code=status)
def outcome(body:dict[str,object],status:int,headers:dict[str,str])->JSONResponse:
    if any(name.lower() in {'content-length','content-type','connection','transfer-encoding','x-content-type-options'} for name in headers): return error('invalid_response_headers',500,'server-owned response header')
    return JSONResponse(body,status_code=status,headers=headers)

async def endpoint(request:Request):
    media=request.headers.get('content-type','').split(';',1)[0].strip().lower()
    if media!='application/json' and not media.endswith('+json'): return error('json_content_type_required',415,'expected application/json')
    declared=request.headers.get('content-length')
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared)>MAX_BODY_BYTES): return error('body_too_large',413,'request body exceeds 16384 bytes')
    raw=await request.body()
    if len(raw)>MAX_BODY_BYTES: return error('body_too_large',413,'request body exceeds 16384 bytes')
    try: parsed=RequestInput.model_validate(json.loads(raw),strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError,UnicodeDecodeError,ValidationError) as exc: return error('invalid_json',400,str(exc))
    return decide(parsed,request)

app.mount('/',StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC,html=True),name='public')

from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid',strict=True); booking_code:str; chilled_crates:int; frozen_crates:int; loading_docks:int; rush_load:bool
def score(chilled_crates:int,frozen_crates:int,loading_docks:int,rush_load:bool)->int:
    total=chilled_crates+frozen_crates; required=chilled_crates*7+frozen_crates*15+(loading_docks*5 if rush_load else 0); capacity=loading_docks*44
    return min(required,capacity)+max(required-capacity,0)*5+(total//6)*8
def calculate(v:RequestInput)->dict[str,object]:
    total=v.chilled_crates+v.frozen_crates; required=v.chilled_crates*7+v.frozen_crates*15+(v.loading_docks*5 if v.rush_load else 0); capacity=v.loading_docks*44; deferred=max(required-capacity,0)
    return {'booking_code':v.booking_code,'shipment_total':total,'cooling_units':required,'dock_capacity_units':capacity,'loaded_units':min(required,capacity),'deferred_units':deferred,'loading_rounds':total//6,'booking_score':score(v.chilled_crates,v.frozen_crates,v.loading_docks,v.rush_load),'booking_state':'booked' if deferred==0 else 'rush_queue' if v.rush_load else 'routine_queue'}
